newsitem.title: GERMANY: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER INTERESTED IN POLITICAL CAREER.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BECKENBAUER INTERESTED IN POLITICAL CAREER.

text.p: Germany's former World Cup-winning captain and coach Franz Beckenbauer has hinted he might be interested in a political career.
Beckenbauer told the German weekly Die Woche that he might be ready to give up his job as chairman of Bayern Munich to take up a post in the German government as Minister for Sport.

"I can deal with people and have never been afraid of taking decisions," he said in an interview to be published on Thursday. "It is time that sport had its own ministry in view of its present importance and social responsibilities."
Sport is presently part of the portfolio of the German Interior Minister.

Beckenbauer, who captained his country to the World Cup in 1974 and coached the Germans to the title in 1990, could be considered for the office since ministers in Germany do not have to be elected members of parliament.
Leading figures in the world game have suggested in the past that 51-year-old Beckenbauer would make a good future president of the world governing body FIFA.

But for the moment his mind is on a leading role in Germany's bid for the 2006 World Cup finals, the same kind of position which France gave to Michel Platini in their successful campaign to host the 1998 tournament.
The "Kaiser" plans to visit Platini in France later this month to get some tips on how the Frenchman sealed the tournament for his country.
